bullets.title: NVDA: Beat-and-raise expected Wednesday; bullish options flow dominant; OpenAI Jalapeño chip a new threat
bullets.body: JPM and UBS both raising NVDA estimates into FQ2:27 earnings (Q beats at $94-95B, guide $107-108B vs buyside); NVDA at decade-low multiples, 75% GMs expected to hold, positioning score max-long. Headwind: OpenAI's Jalapeño ASIC reportedly beats Blackwell on perf/watt and TCO per Reuters/Reuters analysts, though Nvidia's supply chain LTAs and balance sheet cited as durable moat. NVDA options flow most bullish/active this week; SPY only pricing a 1/4pt move for the print vs 1/2pt for Jackson Hole.

bullets.title: INTU: -8.6% after-hours on FY27 guide reset well below consensus
bullets.body: INTU beat Q4 EPS ($4.03 vs $3.58) and revenue ($4.35B vs $4.27B) but FY27 revenue guided $23.3-23.5B vs consensus $23.7B; TurboTax guided $5.38-5.45B vs $5.49B consensus; Q1 operating income guide slashed to $902-915M from $1.47B prior. Key new wrinkle: SBC no longer excluded from non-GAAP starting Aug 1, adding $5.81/share headwind. Citi (Buy) and UBS both flag negative reaction warranted on the guide reset.

bullets.title: MRVL: Assumed Buy at Rosenblatt (PT $300 from $240); custom AI ASIC story seen doubling to $4B by F28
bullets.body: Rosenblatt raises PT to $300 from $240 on buy initiation; JPM sees MRVL custom AI ASIC business more than doubling to $4B by F28 with GOOGL partnership implying ~$20B p.a. run-rate. MRVL options imply 8.8% move with positioning score 1 (light), creating asymmetric setup vs AVGO/NVDA in teens on F28 EPS. Raymond James lists MRVL as top semi pick alongside NVDA, COHR.

bullets.title: AMD: Upgraded to Strong Buy at Raymond James (PT $641 from $565); agentic AI CPU thesis
bullets.body: Raymond James raises AMD to strong buy from outperform, lifting PT to $641 from $565, citing agentic AI as a new CPU growth engine. Separately, INTC x86 share fell below 70% in Q2 2026, with AMD reaching record market share gains driven by AI infrastructure. $3M+ in unusual bullish options prints also detected in AMD today.

bullets.title: SMCI: +3.5% AH on Q2 earnings beat; record revenue and strong data center ramp
bullets.body: SMCI reported record Q2 revenue with gross margin 54.5% vs 53.9% estimate; Q3 guidance $405-415M revenue at 58.3% GM, up meaningfully from Q2. Module business divestiture expected to provide GM tailwind into FY28. UBS flagged as the standout beat in the Tue earnings batch.

bullets.title: PSKY/WBD: M&A speculation lifts PSKY +3.1%; structural remedies in AG suit being discussed
bullets.body: PSKY rose 3.1% after Bloomberg reported parties considering buying Comedy Central from Paramount; bankers approaching buyers for New Line Cinema and WBD cable networks separately. Paramount execs signaling first-ever openness to structural remedies in the AG lawsuit to keep the WBD transaction on track. Ellison (Paramount+) reportedly needs HBO content to be competitive.

bullets.title: AAPL: Surprise Mac Mini (M6, 2nm) and Mac Studio (M5 Ultra) launch; Evercore raises PT to $365
bullets.body: Apple unveiled M6 chip on 2nm process in Mac Mini ($899+) and M5 Ultra Mac Studio ($2,499+) — first 2nm Apple silicon. Evercore ISI reiterates Outperform, raises PT to $365. AAPL traded -0.1% on the day despite launches; stock reaction muted.

bullets.title: OKLO/NNE/SMR/BE: Nuclear and energy tech surge; hyperscaler leased power demand +346% YoY
bullets.body: OKLO +11.5%, BE +6.6%, NNE +5.3%, SMR +8.4% on AI-driven power demand tailwind. SMR announced nuclear-specific AI tools deployment. Jefferies data: non-commenced hyperscaler power leases hit 25.5GW in Q2 (+32% q/q, +346% y/y); ~47% of future hyperscaler capacity planned as leased. China data centers expected to quadruple electricity use by decade end.

bullets.title: DLR: +2% on Singapore 50MW expansion; data center CRE volume +78% YoY to $74.4B
bullets.body: DLR secured 50MW at Jurong Island via Singapore EDB/IMDA deal; July CRE transaction volume jumped 78% YoY to $74.4B with data centers comprising $33.8B (45% of total). Data Center REITs +1.84% on the day, YTD +33.75%.

bullets.title: HOOD: +8.2% as online brokers outperform; AFRM/fintech sector +13% QTD
bullets.body: HOOD surged 8.2%, leading investment bank/broker group as online brokers outperformed on the day. Goldman Sachs Q2 fintech/payments takeaway: group up 13% QTD median; investors hunting names with stronger top-line trends amid decelerating consumer spending.

bullets.title: GOOGL: Waymo testing in Munich; Gemini Enterprise launched for Legal/Financial Services
bullets.body: Waymo (GOOGL subsidiary) to begin autonomous vehicle testing in Munich in coming weeks, expanding international footprint. Google Cloud unveiled Gemini Enterprise AI tools for legal and financial services with partnerships including Weil, Moody's, MSCI, and Relativity. GOOGL down 0.3% on the day.

bullets.title: META: +2.0%; consumer OpenClaw AI agent 'Hatch' weeks away; Watermelon model by October
bullets.body: META gained 2.0% on AI product pipeline news: consumer version of OpenClaw AI agent internally dubbed 'Hatch' expected in coming weeks; Watermelon AI model targeting October launch. Meta's compute optionality highlighted by SemiAnalysis as undervalued at ~$1.5T market cap.

bullets.title: CRM: Q2 earnings Wednesday; consensus $11.33B revenue, $3.27 EPS; options imply 7.7% move
bullets.body: CRM reports Q2 after close Wednesday with consensus expecting $11.33B revenue and $3.27 EPS vs guidance of $11.27-11.35B and $3.25-3.27. Stock +16.6% since May; beat consensus 16 of last 20 revenue quarters and 19 of 20 EPS quarters. Last 4 quarter moves: -1%, +4%, +4%, -5%.

bullets.title: AVGO: Hot Chips die shot consistent with training ASIC architecture; V0 design highly optimized
bullets.body: Broadcom's Hot Chips 2026 presentation showed V0 die shot consistent with a training architecture, described as 'highly optimized to Broadcom's models' by analyst who discussed with the team on-site. Key data point ahead of AVGO preview noted by UBS as financing focus.

bullets.title: MU/SNDK: Memory to represent 68% of CSP capex next year per TrendForce
bullets.body: TrendForce forecasts memory will account for 68% of cloud service provider capex next year. SemiAnalysis notes Nvidia, SK Hynix, and Micron positioned to raise prices as capacity remains constrained. SNDK -0.8% on the day underperformed semis.

bullets.title: NFLX/ROKU: Stratechery explores Netflix potentially selling streaming services as aggregator
bullets.body: Stratechery raised the question of Netflix evolving to sell third-party streaming services, exploring a streamers-as-aggregators model. No directional analyst call attached; flagged as structural theme worth monitoring.

bullets.title: T/VZ: Starlink tracking 1.7M net adds in 3Q vs 2.3M consensus; limited cable threat
bullets.body: KeyBanc Starlink tracker: app downloads +30% YoY but ARPU declining ~16% to $121 and churn abnormally high (56% at T+12). 3Q US net adds tracking ~500K; limited competitive threat to broadband providers. AT&T (OW, $36 PT) and T-Mobile (OW, $250 PT) remain KeyBanc favorites.

bullets.title: AMZN: Raising AI device prices due to chip supply constraints; shifting customers to rental models
bullets.body: Amazon is increasing AI device prices due to chip supply constraints, with the shortage driving a shift toward rental models instead of outright purchases. Major cloud/AI players also reportedly raising equity capital for infrastructure as AI capex requirements exceed self-funding capacity.

bullets.title: UBER: New parental livestream safety feature for teen rides
bullets.body: Uber rolled out a feature enabling parents/guardians to view a live feed from the driver's selfie camera during teenager trips. Product feature news; no financial targets updated.

bullets.title: DKNG: 25% of Gen Z treat sports betting as deliberate part of long-term financial plan
bullets.body: Bloomberg reports 25% of Gen Z incorporate sports betting into long-term financial planning per new data — a secular demand tailwind for DraftKings. No analyst action attached.
